angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 910,671 km at 131.78 pc = 0.09 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.5884 +/- 0.0117 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 131.78 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.309 +/- 0.059 solar radii from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-4495 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..135W/abstract): 910,671 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.247 +/- 0.045 solar masses from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-4495 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..135W/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6210 +/- 70 K from Wang et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4495 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..135W/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Wang et al. 2026, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-4495 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..135W/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-4495.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.300, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
